title: Efficiency of Anticoagulation and Thrombosis Prophylaxis in the Intensive Care Unit
summary: Critically ill patients are at high risk for developing thromboses. Effective protection and early detection of these complications are therefore of great importance. If blood thinning is necessary for the treatment of thromboses, this patient group is also particularly at risk for complications. Prevention of thrombosis and controlled anticoagulation are two important pillars in the care of intensive care patients. This study examines the rate of thromboses and the frequency of complications caused by the necessary blood thinning in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit before and after the introduction of a new standard.
conditions: Haemorrhage and haematoma complicating a procedure, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Critically ill patients are retrospectively and prospectively evaluated for the efficacy of anticoagulation and thrombosis prophylaxis in the intensive care unit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treatment in the intensive care unit 
Drug-based thrombosis prophylaxis or anticoagulation
Exclusion criteria:
Length of stay at ICU <48h
